newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MAS says to add 10 pct to workforce.
newsitem.headline: MAS says to add 10 pct to workforce.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said on Sunday it plans to employ an additional 2,000 workers this year, increasing its workforce by 10 percent.
Most of the additional staff would be cabin and technical crew, MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli told a news conference.

"On our plans this year, slightly above 2,000 new employees will be added to the existing staff, so that we'll go from 20,000 to 22,000. These are mainly cabin crew as well as technical crew," he said.
The airline will move to the new and larger Kuala Lumpur International Airport which will be ready by next year.
The company is building three major facilities at the nine-billion ringgit ($3.62 billion) airport -- catering, cargo and engineering facilities.
MAS on Sunday announced a 3.271 billion ringgit cash-raising exercise to help finance its 10 billion ringgit purchase of 25 Boeing Co aircraft and for investment at the new airport.
Tajudin said some one billion ringgit of the money raised would be channeled to its airport projects.
The catering facilities will be able to prepare 35,000 meals a day, he said.
Its advanced cargo centre will be able to handle an annual 650,000 tonnes of throughput a year, and which could be raised to one million tonnes.
The company will also operate a flight control centre at the main terminal building, Tajudin said.
